newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania to appeal for IBCA rating upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania to appeal for IBCA rating upgrade.

text.p: Lithuanian Finance Minister Rolandas Matiliauskas said on Thursday he will travel to London next week to ask the IBCA credit rating agency for a higher rating than Lithuania was given by Moody's.
Matiliauskas will meet IBCA officials on January 20.
"The aim of the visit is to take part in an IBCA meeting and appeal to IBCA to give us a better credit rating," Matiliauskas told Reuters.
He said the current IBCA rating, which has not been published but given only to the Lithuanians, was the same as that given by Moody's.
Last year Moody's rated Lithuanian foreign currency debt as Ba2 and the country's bank deposits at Ba3. It was the first international credit rating for a former Soviet country.
"In their opinion, there were no changes for the better during the year and we think that the situation is getting better," Matiliauskas said.
He is part of a new right-wing led government that took power in November 1996 and has said it will be more reformist than its ex-Communist predecessors.
Lithuania was hit by a bank crisis at the end of 1995 but confidence in the banking sector has been improving.
